subject: Falcon Health — hosted API data lifecycle questions (data residency / retention / deletion)
message_1_body:
Marissa —

Thanks for taking this early. Falcon Health is working through vendor security for our new patient-facing pilot and we need clarifications on a few hosted-API items around where data lives and how fast it can be deleted. High level questions below; we attached our short SQ template. Can you confirm?

1) In which AWS regions do you store raw request/response payloads for hosted customers by default? Do you offer region binding (we need US-West or EU only for PHI)?
2) What is the default retention for request payloads (human text) vs. structured logs vs. audit logs and backups? Give exact windows and any exceptions.
3) If we request an immediate tenant data purge, what is the operational workflow and expected completion SLA across replicas and caches? Is there an API-driven option we can call?
4) Are backups / snapshots retained separately from primary store? If so, what is their retention and how are they removed on deletion requests?
5) What logs/evidence can you provide for us to satisfy our InfoSec questionnaire (attestation, screenshots, download of deletion job ids)?

Attached is our 2-page SQ. We appreciate concise answers we can put in our security review.

—Sheldon Park
Dir. Information Security, Falcon Health
message_2_subject: Re: Hosted API data lifecycle questions
message_2_body:
Hi Sheldon —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. Below are concise, actionable answers you can paste into the SQ. I also attached a one-page PDF with the same responses and a small evidence bundle (screenshots of retention settings and an example deletion job id). If you want, we can follow with a short 30-minute call to walk through the process with infra.

Summary answers (hosted API):

- Region / residency: By default hosted customer request payloads and derived artifacts are stored in the region backing the customer account. For new US customers default is us-west-2 (Oregon). We support region binding: we can provision your tenant data to us-west-2 only or to eu-west-1 on request (regional binding requires an explicit contract flag).

- Retention windows (defaults):
  • Request payloads (raw text): 30 days by default for troubleshooting/eval pipelines.
  • Structured operational logs (token counts, route metrics): 90 days.
  • Audit logs (access records, config changes): 365 days.
  • Backups / snapshots: rolling snapshot retention is 14 days; longer retention is available via an add-on.

- Immediate purge workflow (what happens when you request deletion):
  1) Customer submits deletion request via Support Portal or DELETE API (we provide a tenant-level API: DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data).
  2) Deletion job enters our orchestration queue and parallel purge tasks are issued to every regional replica and to cache layers (prefix/KV caches, GPU session caches).
  3) Primary store objects are deleted within 24 hours; cache eviction + background GC completes within 72 hours in typical cases.
  4) Snapshot/backups are scheduled for scrub; snapshot catalog entries are removed and underlying blocks are zeroed/overwritten within 14 days (per snapshot retention policy).
  5) We provide a deletion job id and an audit record (job id, timestamps, operator id) and can deliver that to your security team.

- Backups: yes, snapshots are separate. Snapshots are immutable for the snapshot retention window and are scrubbed by the snapshot lifecycle process when retention expires or when a tenant-level purge is requested (subject to the snapshot scrub window above).

- Evidence for SQ:
  • We attach a PDF (Falcon_SQ_Responses_v1.pdf) with the canonical answers.
  • Evidence bundle (redwood-data-retention-evidence-2028-05.zip) contains example deletion job id, screenshot of tenant region setting (us-west-2), and a sample audit log entry.
  • We can provide an export of audit logs for the deletion request and a signed attestation statement (SOC2 linkage) on request.

Notes / exceptions:
- System-generated backups used for disaster recovery may have replication copies in multiple AZs within the region; we do not replicate hosted customer raw payloads to a different AWS region without explicit configuration.
- Legal holds / subpoena may temporarily prevent deletion for the service of a lawful process; in that case we will notify you and follow the lawful process playbook.

Next steps: If this is good, I can: 1) attach these answers to the SQ you sent, 2) schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with infra to demonstrate a purge, or 3) start the paperwork to enable region binding to us-west-2 only. Which do you prefer?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

message_3_subject: Internal: confirm scrub SLA and backup scrub flow
message_3_body:
Marissa / Karthik —

Quick follow-up before we send the final: can infra confirm two specifics so we don't overpromise to Falcon?

1) The 24-hour primary delete window — is that 'best effort' for large tenants (>500GB) or guaranteed?
2) Backup snapshot scrub: we say 'within 14 days' — is there a queued GC dependency that could extend that to 21 days in edge cases?

If either could slip, let's provide a clear note in the PDF and offer a remediation plan (accelerated snapshot scrub for enterprise customers as an add-on). I can attach the example deletion job export when infra gives the job id.

message_4_subject: Re: Hosted API data lifecycle questions — confirmation and next steps
message_4_body:
Hi Sheldon —

Following up with engineering confirmation and a short clarifying note for the SQ. Two small clarifications to Marissa's answers above:

• Primary delete SLA: for standard hosted tenants the orchestration initiates and removes primary store objects within 24 hours; for very large datasets (>500GB) deletion may take longer due to object-level GC. In those cases we commit to a maximum of 72 hours to complete primary-store deletions, and we will surface a deletion job id throughout the process.

• Snapshot/backups scrub: snapshots are scheduled for lifecycle deletion and are typically removed within 14 days. In rare edge cases where snapshot GC work is queued behind a region-wide maintenance window, scrub may extend to 21 days. For Falcon Health we can add an accelerated snapshot-scrub SLA as part of the procurement attachment (we'll include an addendum in the contract).

To keep this simple for your InfoSec checklist, we propose the following wording you can paste into your SQ fields: 

"Redwood Inference (hosted API) stores customer request payloads in the customer's designated region (default us-west-2 for US customers). Default retention windows are 30 days for raw request payloads, 90 days for structured operational logs, 365 days for audit logs, and 14 days for rolling backups. Customers may request immediate tenant-level deletion via Support Portal or tenant API (DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data). Primary store deletions complete within 24–72 hours depending on dataset size; cache eviction finishes within 72 hours; snapshot scrub completes within 14 days (up to 21 days in rare maintenance-edge cases). Deletion job ids and signed attestation for completed purges are available on request. Legal holds will be handled per lawful process and will be communicated to the customer."

Next steps we propose:
1) I'll attach the finalized PDF and evidence bundle to the HubSpot deal (linked).
2) Marissa — please schedule a 30-minute demo with Falcon (I recommend 05/30 if available).
3) If Falcon wants region binding + accelerated snapshot scrub, we can add that to the deal as an SLA addendum and include pricing.

Sheldon — let me know if that language answers the SQ or if you want tighter windows; we're happy to provide an addendum for procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Lead, Platform Reliability
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
